To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
estrogen agonists can be identified in the uterus and that these agonists are likely to contribute to the pathogenesis of uterine leiomiomas.
xenoestrogeneic compounds can activate the estrogen receptor in the uterine smooth muscle and that this activation is predictive of estrogen-like activity in vivo.
the effects of xenoestrogenic ligands in the uterine smooth muscle are predicted by the activation of the AF2 domain of the estrogen receptor.
In summary, our research is concerned with
identifying the mechanism by which environmental estrogens may impact the uterine smooth muscle.
the effects of endocrine-disrupting compounds on the myometrium, a tissue that has received little attention in the context of endocrine disruption.
the effects of xenoestrogen on uterine smooth muscle, and the mechanism of action of these compounds.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the AF2 activation function of the ER is a useful tool for identifying estrogenic activity of xenoestrogenic compounds in uterine smooth muscle cells.
the AF2 function is necessary but not sufficient for ER-mediated agonism in uterine smooth muscle cells.
AF2 activation is necessary, but not sufficient, for xenoestrogen agonist activity in the myometrial cell line and that AF2 activation may predict agonist activity in uterine tissues in vivo.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the activation of ER AF2 is predictive of estrogenic agonist activity in the myometrial tissues and may be a useful tool in identifying potential environmental endocrine disrupters.
AF2 activation predicts the agonist activity of ER ligands, both natural and synthetic, in the myometrial cell and intact uterine myoepithelium.
the activation function AF2 of the estrogen receptor is a key component of the mechanism by which xenoestrogene agonists exert their biological effects.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the ER is not just a receptor for estrogen, but a receptor that can bind and be activated by a wide variety of chemicals.
the myometrium, like other tissues, can be used to predict the effects that a particular ligand will have in vivo.
the uterine smooth muscle is a target of xenoestrogen action, and that the mechanism of action is via AF2 activation.
